name: Cartouche — Corporate Vanity Public Sculpture Audit
creator: Benedikta Farooq-Achebe
description: A long-running art project in which Farooq-Achebe identifies corporate-commissioned public sculptures across GLMZ and installs small bronze plaques on them — indistinguishable in style from official civic plaques — that replace the original dedication text with accurate descriptions of what the commissioning corponation was under investigation for at the time the sculpture was funded. The plaques are installed overnight and have proven nearly impossible to remove without damaging the original sculptures. Over ninety plaques have been installed since 2203.
cultural_impact: Created a lasting secondary text layer on corporate public art across the city that has never been fully eradicated; art historians now routinely document both the original dedications and Farooq-Achebe's plaques as part of GLMZ's cultural record.
controversy: Farooq-Achebe was sued for vandalism seven times and acquitted on six; the seventh case is ongoing after a plaque was installed on a sculpture in a Tier 4 district where the corponation has judicial influence.
story_hooks: A character is commissioned — by whom, they're not sure — to find and remove a specific plaque before a corporate delegation visits the sculpture in two days.

Farooq-Achebe has gone silent and a new plaque has appeared that accuses a corponation of something that hasn't been made public yet — suggesting either an incredible source or a dangerous fabrication.
A collector is paying extraordinary sums for the original bronze plaques that have been successfully removed, and the buyer's motive is unclear — preservation, or erasure?
